topic: Research: Claude Mythos API Access Guide 2026: How to Get In

key_points: Positions Mythos 5 access as restricted rather than self-serve and warns builders not to design around unofficial workarounds.
Explains that Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are the same underlying model class under different policy/safeguard profiles.
Recommends production model routing that treats Fable 5 or Opus 4.8 as the practical default while Mythos remains gated.
Official launch post: Fable 5 is broadly available while Mythos 5 is limited to Glasswing partners and select research programs.
States both models are priced at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.
Frames Mythos 5 as a model with lifted safeguards for specific high-risk domains, not a normal public Claude tier.
Developer-facing doc lists model IDs, API behavior, availability, context window, output limits, and supported features.
Says Mythos 5 is limited availability through Project Glasswing and access should go through Anthropic, AWS, or Google Cloud account teams.
Highlights integration differences: adaptive thinking is always on, raw chain of thought is not returned, and Fable refusals/fallback handling must be implemented.
Explains why Mythos Preview was gated: cybersecurity capability can help defenders but also raises misuse risk.
Identifies Project Glasswing as Anthropic's vehicle for vetted cyberdefense access.
Useful background for access criteria: defensive security, critical software, vulnerability discovery, disclosure, and patching.
Third-party security-industry analysis of Mythos Preview and Project Glasswing.
Emphasizes that Mythos is general-purpose but notable for cybersecurity capability discovered during testing.
Frames the likely enterprise buyer concern: how to benefit from advanced vulnerability discovery while avoiding unsafe deployment patterns.

stats.fact: As of Anthropic's June 12, 2026 statement, Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access was disabled for all customers to comply with a U.S. export-control directive covering foreign nationals; other Anthropic models were not affected.
Claude Mythos 5 is not generally available; approved customers must go through Project Glasswing and contact their Anthropic, AWS, or Google Cloud account team.
Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 share a 1 million token context window and support up to 128k output tokens per request.
Published Claude pricing lists Claude Mythos 5 limited availability at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, with prompt caching and batch pricing also listed.
AWS lists Claude Mythos Preview as a gated research preview launched April 7, 2026, with access prioritized for defensive cybersecurity use cases.
Google Cloud announced Claude Mythos Preview private preview on Vertex AI on April 8, 2026 for a select group of customers as part of Project Glasswing.
Anthropic said Project Glasswing started with roughly 50 initial partners, later expanded to approximately 150 new organizations in more than 15 countries, each subject to security requirements.
Anthropic reported that early Project Glasswing partners found more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity security flaws while using Mythos Preview to scan codebases.
Anthropic's June 12 statement says pre-launch red teaming involved the U.S. government, UK AISI, private third parties, and internal teams for thousands of total hours.
Anthropic said it had not found a universal jailbreak for Fable 5 at the time of the June 12 access suspension statement.

angles: Lead with the access reality: there is no public Claude Mythos API signup path; the current path is vetted Project Glasswing or future trusted-access programs.
Add a June 2026 access status box: Fable 5/Mythos 5 launch, limited availability, then U.S. export-control suspension and why teams must re-check availability before planning.
Separate Mythos Preview, Mythos 5, and Fable 5 so readers do not confuse private preview, limited-release lifted-safeguard access, and the broader safeguarded model.

Explain what an application should contain: defensive cybersecurity or approved research use case, critical-infrastructure relevance, security controls, data-retention acceptance, disclosure/patching process, and account-team sponsorship.
Give developers a practical fallback architecture: model abstraction layer, Claude Fable/Opus fallback, refusal handling, prompt-cache cost awareness, and feature flags for restricted models.
Warn against gray-market access, leaked endpoints, third-party vendor claims, and scraping model IDs; the credible route is account-team approval.
Make U.S.-only inference and foreign-national restrictions a compliance checklist item for companies with global teams.
Position Mythos access as a governance process, not just an API key request: legal, security, vendor risk, and incident response should be ready before applying.
